purpose: The step 4 amendment: the first run of the price-class bridge. It fixes the snapshot and its pins, the universe, the R4 disappearance events and their last-close rerun, the missingness refusals and reporting, the classes and signals, the sleeves, the stock and switch costs, R0, rule R1, and R2 on the sleeves, the benchmarks, the metrics, the survival and transmission metrics, the halves and the comparison window, the S4 tests and their BY family, the prior exposures, the decision outcomes, and the required tests for the step 4 code. It is committed alone, before any step 4 code, sleeve, return, IC, or rule weight exists.

revision_history.reason: Freeze review round 1 repairs before any step 4 result: OPUS-S4F-M1 (long-only Sharpe subtracts the French RF), OPUS-S4F-M2 option (a) (rule R1 sigma is the sleeve's own daily volatility; active-risk weighting dropped), GPT-S4-FR1-A1 and OPUS-S4F-A2 (terminal-free segment loader), GPT-S4-FR1-A2 and OPUS-S4F-A1 (missingness span, denominator, and unresolved and unknown exit classes), GPT-S4-FR1-A3 (affected-event observation time and counting unit), OPUS-S4F-A3 (the last-close rerun computes no p-value), OPUS-S4F-A4 (static-cohort record), OPUS-S4F-A5 (comparison-window rationale), OPUS-S4F-A6 (seal-gap stops), and OPUS-S4F-A7 (records wording and the closure adapter).

naming: Rule R1 means the inverse-volatility rule and invariant R1 means the AGENTS.md timing invariant. R0 and rule R1 here are the step 2 rules applied to the six stock-level sleeves; rule R1's sigma is the volatility of each sleeve's own return, as in step 2, and only its window changes (126 daily rows instead of 36 monthly returns). R2 is the step 3 rule with its step 3 multipliers.

sections: rules.R0 and rules.R1 on stock-level sleeves (rule R1 sigma window)
costs (stock costs inside sleeves; drift-adjusted class turnover)
step 4 tests, decision outcomes, and required tests (new)

authority: The v1 amendment_policy covers only the v2 amendment; amendments 1 and 2 were coordinator defaults outside that list, and this amendment is recorded the same way. v1 step2_decision_rule.scope leaves 'the implementable check on the repository's point-in-time S&P 500 books' to step 4; this amendment defines that check. Owner decisions O-5 (local reads of the snapshots for step 4; aggregates and hashed manifests only) and O-9 (premise VP-2 re-ratified under DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY for step 4) and the coordinator scope defaults of 2026-09-29 in docs/decision_log.md bind it. Each choice listed under technical_defaults is a coordinator technical default under the AGENTS.md Owner Process Constraints, logged in docs/decision_log.md; none loosens R1, R2, R4, R6, R8, or R9. No public-data definition, result, or decision of steps 2 and 3 changes.

question_and_decision.question: On long-only top-quintile point-in-time S&P 500 books after costs, does rule R1 (step 2's inverse-volatility rule, with a daily window) still beat R0, and does R2 still avoid losing to rule R1? How much of the public long-short result survives?
question_and_decision.decides: the stock-level baseline product (rule R1 or R0), whether R2 continues, and the survival figure the owner uses before step 4b (SEC as-filed classes) and step 5
question_and_decision.looks: One declared run: the primary run under the R4 adverse default and its last-close rerun, both computed and reported together. A rerun happens only to fix a defect; every attempt is appended to reports/m5_step4_attempts.jsonl and stays visible under R9.

snapshot.only_snapshot: Step 4 reads real_v2 only. real_v1 is not opened; real_v2's post side serves the same local acquisitions (docs/engineering_log.md, 2026-09-28 M4.8 Stage D entry).
snapshot.location: Passed to the runner as a command-line snapshot directory. The repository names the private data root only through the environment variable EFR_EODHD_DATA_DIR and the snapshot only by its id; no private path is written to the repository or to a report (R11).

pins.files: manifest.json, panel/inventory_discovery.json, holdout_seal_v2.json, membership/membership_build_manifest.json, membership/constituent_intervals.csv, identity/interval_results.csv, and identity/security_master.csv under the snapshot root. discovery_inputs_sha256 is recomputed by research/m4_7_universe_build.py discovery_inputs_sha256 and must also equal the value recorded in the inventory and the build manifest; it covers the curated membership files and membership/identity_boundaries.csv. interval_results_sha256 equals the build manifest's recorded output hash for that file.
pins.panel_files: every panel file named by the pinned inventory must match its recorded SHA-256 before any load, as in bind_snapshot_v3

declared_properties.seal_window: [2019-07-31, 2020-07-31), from the pinned seal carry record

snapshot.binding: A new bind_step4 keeps every check of research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py bind_snapshot_v3 that precedes a panel load (snapshot open, partition rule, snapshot id, the pins above, the recomputed discovery inputs, every panel hash, the seal carry window, the calendar source, and _refuse_split_sources) and drops the census JSON and the terminal projection checks, because step 4 accepts no terminal evidence. Any mismatch refuses the run before a panel is loaded.
snapshot.loader: A new load_segment_runs_step4 is research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py load_segment_runs without its read_engine_events call: it reads the pinned interval CSV and security master, runs _refuse_split_sources again before each load, opens through load_eod_cohort_panels only the panel files of the segment's side that the pinned inventory names, and sets each segment's events to an empty frame with the engine's terminal-event columns. It reads nothing under terminal/, and no terminal projection or placeholder file is created in the snapshot.
snapshot.seal_guard: research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py _segment_calendar raises seal_bracket_computation_forbidden when any loaded field row lies on the other side or in the seal window; bind_step4 raises holdout_overlap_refused when the seal carry window differs from the declared seal_window. The only panel files the loader opens are the inventory's files for the segment's own side, so no seal-window partition is opened. The seal window stays unaccessed.
snapshot.writes: The runner writes nothing inside the snapshot; its outputs are reports/m5_step4.md, reports/m5_step4.json, and reports/m5_step4_attempts.jsonl, which carry aggregates and hashes only: no raw provider row, provider response, membership list, security code, or private path (R11).

segments.source: research/m4_7_universe_build.py discovery_segments on the pinned calendar, holdout window, and d0_pre; the runner recomputes them and refuses (census_runner_inconsistency:segment_rows) when they differ from these dates

universe.membership: Point-in-time constituent intervals from the pinned interval CSV, resolved by src/backtest/portfolio.py resolve_pit_universe_mask, and the causal eligibility mask research/m4_7_common_support.py causal_support_schedule (causal_signal_eligibility_mask_v3: E(r - 1) = S_mask(r - 1)). Members later removed, acquired, or bankrupt stay in the universe for the days they were members (invariant R2).
universe.identity: Permanent IDs from the snapshot build under rules E1 to E6 and curated_identity_boundary_v1; an ambiguous identity was refused at build time and is never stitched (R3).
universe.assets: Per segment, the permanent IDs with an interval and a panel on that segment's side, excluding SPY.US#E1, as in prepare_segment. A member without a panel on the side, and every interval the build left unresolved, is unpriced: it is never held, so it is outside every sleeve, the equal-weight benchmark, and the R4 affected-event count; its member-days are counted (missingness.unpriced_share).

returns_and_volume.return_basis: Vendor adjusted_close is the only return basis (R5), through research/real_data_multifactor_diagnostic.py build_adjusted_research_panels; no cash dividend is added. Premise VP-2 (the vendor's adjusted close applies each declared distribution) holds under owner decision O-9 for step 4 only; the report header discloses VP-2 and the M4.8 census share (S_D > 0.05 on 22.5 percent of eligible member-days).
returns_and_volume.dollar_volume: Split-only close times vendor volume (build_adjusted_research_panels), the R7 basis used by AMIHUD_ILLIQ_63.
returns_and_volume.benchmark_series: SPY.US#E1 adjusted close; a segment whose SPY series is not finite on every row refuses (prepare_segment).
returns_and_volume.risk_free: French FF3 monthly RF (french_ff3_monthly, column RF, divided by 100) from the pinned public cache of reports/m5_public_data_manifest.json, used only in the long-only Sharpe (metrics.sharpe_long_only). A comparison or sleeve month without an RF value refuses.

disappearances.accepted_evidence: None. Stage E never ran, and the 68 in-scope terminal candidates are uncurated. The runner passes no snapshot terminal event to the engine.
disappearances.residual_stops: Per segment, research/m4_7_common_support.py residual_disappearances(schedule, bars, accepted = empty set, candidates) finds every stop of an asset that is potentially held (P_r of potentially_held, which depends on no factor): part 1 takes each delisting-candidate settlement row (last bar + 1) from the security master, part 2 each asset whose last bar precedes the segment's last book row.
disappearances.seal_gap_stops: A pre-side piece whose bars end at a seal gap before the pre segment's last book row becomes a part 2 stop, although the build types such a piece as ending by identity split (research/m4_7_universe_build.py seal_gap_identity_split). Its cause is unknown to step 4, so it takes the same -100 percent default. These stops are identified by the piece's interval exit class seal_gap_identity_split and counted separately in the affected-event table.
disappearances.primary_events: residual_bound_events (residual_disappearance_minus_100pct_bound_v1): each residual stop settles at terminal_return -1.0 at its stop row, with reference and known_at at the preceding observed row. This replaces the refusal residual_unevidenced_disappearance of prepare_segment. It is the R4 side-aware adverse default for a long position with an unknown cause; step 4 holds no short position.
disappearances.same_events_everywhere: The same event set enters every sleeve, every cost case, and the equal-weight benchmark of that segment. The engine applies an event only to a position held at the stop, and the universe mask removes the asset from its effective date on, so no book sells before the stop.
disappearances.last_close_rerun: A second full run replaces every terminal_return with 0.0 (settlement at the last observed close) and recomputes sleeves, the equal-weight benchmark, sigma, R0, rule R1, R2, the metrics, survival, transmission, and the S4 mean differences. It computes no S4 p-value, q-value, or interval: the rerun is a sensitivity case for fragility, not a tested variant.
disappearances.fragility: For each S4 mean difference and each closure margin (the 8 of rule R1 against R0, the 8 of R2 against rule R1, and, when R0 is the point-in-time baseline, the 8 of R2 against R0), sign(x) is -1, 0, or +1, with |x| < 1e-12 counted as 0. The result is labeled fragile when any of these signs, or any decision outcome, differs between the primary run and the last-close rerun. The label is reported in the header and beside the decision; it does not change the decision, which uses the primary run.

affected_events.event: one residual stop: a permanent ID and its stop row s
affected_events.sleeve_and_benchmark: For each sleeve and cost case and for the equal-weight benchmark: the number of events that settle a held position, and the sum and maximum of their incoming weights, where the incoming weight is the engine's settlement-log incoming_weight, the position's share of the book's gross capital at the close of row s - 1.
affected_events.rule: For R0, rule R1, and R2 at each cost case: the rule's incoming weight for an event is the sum over the sleeves holding it of (the sleeve's share of rule capital at the close of row s - 1) x (the sleeve's incoming weight). The sleeve's share is w_s,t * G_s / (sum over j of w_j,t * G_j), where w_s,t is the month-t target weight and G_j is sleeve j's gross growth from the month-(t-1) close to the close of row s - 1. The switch cost is taken from rule capital at the month-(t-1) close and scales every sleeve alike, so it leaves the shares unchanged.
affected_events.counting: At rule level each event counts once, however many sleeves hold it (unique events); the number of sleeve-event incidences is reported beside it.
affected_events.classes: Every count is also split into seal-gap stops and other residual stops.
affected_events.runs: reported for both the primary run and the last-close rerun

missingness.halts: missing_price_policy halt_gap_return_v1 (src/backtest/portfolio.py _halt_gap_returns): a held asset whose bar is absent keeps its mark and returns 0, and realizes its gap return at its next close; unmarked halt rows and locked capital are typed and counted per sleeve. An absent bar is a halt, not bad data; a present close that is not finite positive refuses (incoming_price_invalid), and the loader rejects non-finite or non-positive raw prices before panel construction (src/data/parquet_loader.py).
refusals: a snapshot pin, panel hash, discovery-inputs, seal carry, calendar source, or segment-row mismatch, or a split table beside a panel
a loaded field row on the other side or in the seal window (seal_bracket_computation_forbidden)
a segment whose SPY series is not finite on every row

an engine Class I reason (incoming_price_invalid, execution_price_invalid, terminal_target_invalid, terminal_events_invalid, unresolved_disappearance, terminal_reference_bar_missing), including a held close that is present but not finite positive
an empty sleeve target at any scheduled rebalance of a segment: no eligible member has a finite signal, so the engine would silently hold cash (src/backtest/portfolio.py _build_target_weights)
a zero or non-finite rule R1 sigma for a sleeve in a comparison month
a missing R2 multiplier for one of the four themes in a comparison month
a missing sleeve or benchmark monthly return in a sleeve month
a missing French RF value in a comparison or sleeve month
missingness.typed_and_counted: An eligible member without a finite signal at a signal row (warm-up or a missing anchor) is not ranked; its count per sleeve and rebalance is reported. Nothing is filled, clipped, dropped silently, or repaired (R6).

unpriced_share.accounting_span: per segment, the calendar rows from its first reset row through its last book row
unpriced_share.member_day: a pair (interval, calendar row) with the row inside the accounting span and inside the interval under the build's interval semantics (half_open_start_inclusive_end_exclusive_v1, calendar_row_semantics_v1). When intervals of one vendor code overlap, the row counts once, under the lowest interval_id.
unpriced_share.denominator: every member-day of every interval in the pinned identity/interval_results.csv (848 intervals at Stage D), resolved or not
unpriced_share.priced: a member-day of a resolved interval whose permanent ID has a panel on the segment's side
unpriced_share.unpriced: every other member-day: a resolved interval without a side panel, or an unresolved interval
unpriced_share.exit_class_split: the unpriced member-days by class: the interval's recorded exit_class (index_removal_still_trading, delisting_candidate, disappearance_outside_membership, seal_gap_identity_split) for a resolved interval; unresolved_no_permanent_id for an unresolved interval; unknown for a resolved interval whose exit class is blank or outside that list
unpriced_share.reason_split: the unpriced member-days by reason: EOD quarantine, episode panel refusal, identity refusal (ambiguous reuse), no vendor bars, no bars in the interval, entry_missing_field, or other
unpriced_share.reconciliation: priced plus unpriced equals the denominator, and each split sums to the unpriced total; any difference refuses the run
unpriced_share.other_exposure_by_exit_class: The signal-exclusion counts (typed_and_counted) and the unmarked halt rows per sleeve are also split by the held or excluded member's interval exit class, with the same classes.
unpriced_share.placement: The unpriced share of each segment is printed beside every excess figure over SPY and over the equal-weight benchmark.
unpriced_share.stage_d_count: At D0_pre, 111 of 448 members have no pre-side panel.

classes_and_signals.signals: The six frozen Family A signals of research/m4_7_family_a.py family_a_signals on adjusted_close, SPY.US#E1, and dollar_volume, masked by S_mask; every signal reads higher is better (LOW_VOL_252 and LOW_BETA_252 negated).
classes_and_signals.map_source: the nearest JKP characteristic named in research/factor_catalog.csv (rows repo.MOM_12_1 to repo.AMIHUD_ILLIQ_63) and its cluster in data/public_cache/jkp_cluster_labels.csv at the v1 pinned commit
classes_and_signals.waiting: Seasonality has no price signal in Family A, and share-based Size needs shares data; both wait. The SEC as-filed value and quality classes are step 4b.
classes_and_signals.class_return: Descriptive only: the class return of theme k in month t is rule R1 within the class, the sum over its sleeves of (1/sigma_s,t) * r_s,t divided by the sum of 1/sigma_s,t, with the rule R1 sigma below. A one-sleeve class equals its sleeve.

sleeves.count: One sleeve per signal and segment: 6 signals x 2 segments, each at 2 cost cases, in each of the two event runs.
sleeves.engine_call: research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py run_book('long_only', prices, signal, calendar, window = (anchor_row, last_book_row), intervals, events, cost, top_pct = 0.20, missing_price_policy = 'halt_gap_return_v1'), with the segment's residual events, one engine call per segment from its anchor row, starting from cash.
sleeves.holdings: At each scheduled month-end rebalance, the ceil(0.2 * n) highest-signal names among the n eligible members with a finite signal, equal weight (src/backtest/portfolio.py _select_top_assets). Ties at the cutoff follow the engine's stable sort in asset-column order.
sleeves.timing: The engine contract after_close_signal_next_observed_close_v1 with signal_lag_periods 1: the rebalance row r is the last trading day of a month, the signal and eligibility use row r - 1, the target executes at the close of row r, and it first earns the return of row r + 1.
sleeves.monthly_return: The sleeve's month-t net return is the product over calendar rows in (last trading day of t-1, last trading day of t] of (1 + daily net return), minus 1. The first sleeve month of each segment also includes the first reset row, which carries the cost of the initial purchase. The benchmark monthly returns compound the same way.
sleeves.sleeve_months: pre 2014-05 to 2019-06 (62 months); post 2021-09 to 2026-07 (59 months). The partial month 2026-08 (five rows to 2026-08-07) enters no monthly figure and is counted.
sleeves.active_return: The sleeve's month-t net active return is its monthly net return minus the equal-weight benchmark's monthly return in the same event run; it is a reported metric and no rule input.

costs.stock_costs: Inside each sleeve, the engine's transaction_cost_bps and slippage_bps on traded notional, booked on the execution row: primary 1 + 4 bp, sensitivity 2 + 8 bp (research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py REGISTERED costs). No zero-cost sleeve is run; a zero-cost figure, if shown, is labeled a gross diagnostic.
costs.switch_cost: The class layer pays 20 bp (primary) or 50 bp (sensitivity) on drift-adjusted class turnover: turnover_t = sum over sleeves s of |w_s,t - wd_s,t-1|, where wd_s,t-1 = w_s,t-1 * (1 + r_s,t-1) / (1 + sum over j of w_j,t-1 * r_j,t-1) is last month's weight after its month-(t-1) net return. The first comparison month of each segment starts from cash, so its turnover is 1. Net class-layer return: r_net,t = sum over s of w_s,t * r_s,t - (bps / 10000) * turnover_t, with r_s,t the sleeve's net monthly return.
costs.booking: Stock costs on the execution row inside the sleeve; switch costs recorded at the month-(t-1) close and deducted from the month-t return, as in step 2.
costs.netting: Nothing nets across sleeves: two sleeves trading the same name in opposite directions both pay, which overstates costs; the report says so.
costs.borrow: Step 4 holds no short position, so no borrow cost applies.
costs.impact: No market-impact model (the M4.8 engine setting 'none'); the report states it.

rules.set: The six sleeves of a segment, all present in every comparison month.

R1.weights: w_s,t proportional to 1/sigma_s,t, normalized, no cap (rule_weights 'R1').
R1.sigma: the sample standard deviation (ddof 1) of the sleeve's own daily net return over the 126 calendar rows (US trading days of the SPY calendar) ending on the last trading day of month t-2, counted from the row after the segment's first reset row; each cost case uses its own sleeve returns and each event run its own series. This is step 2's sigma (the volatility of the member's own return) with a 126-row daily window in place of 36 monthly returns.
R1.undefined: a month whose window has fewer than 126 rows has no rule R1 weight; a zero or non-finite sigma in a comparison month refuses
R1.no_variant: No active-risk or other sigma variant is run, reported, or tested.

R2.weights: w2_s,t = w1_s,t * M_k(s),t / (sum over j of w1_j,t * M_k(j),t), with k(s) the sleeve's theme (research/m5_step3.py tilt with every sleeve in the block).
R2.multipliers: M_k,t is the amendment 3 R2 class multiplier of theme k for return month t, taken unchanged from research/m5_step3.py r2_on_months on jkp_factors_153 with the pinned public inputs of reports/m5_public_data_manifest.json (SHA-256 ba025b1a67af175dfff892c3dcefe96b573f7542b6d365dcdc783353c2af998f at the base), for the themes Momentum, Short-Term Reversal, Low Risk, and Size. They are not re-estimated on the stock-level books.
R2.label: R2 keeps the step 3 label 'no evidence of state timing'; step 4 makes no state-timing claim.

rules.timing: Every class-layer input for month t ends at month t-2: sleeve daily returns through the last trading day of month t-2, and the R2 multipliers, whose inputs end at t-2 (French data) and t-3 (FRED). The class weights execute at the close of the last trading day of month t-1 and earn the sleeves' month-t returns (invariant R1; the step 2 event order of amendment 2). The RF of month t enters only the Sharpe metric, an outcome.
rules.start: In each segment the class layer starts at the first month t whose sigma window has 126 rows for every sleeve; R0, rule R1, and R2 all start that month from cash. Expected from the calendar alone: 2014-12 in the pre segment and 2022-05 in the post segment.

benchmarks.spy: SPY.US#E1 adjusted close, cost-free, compounded monthly as the sleeves are
benchmarks.equal_weight_pit: research/m4_7_sp500_pit_rerun.py run_book('long_only') with equal_weight_signal on the evaluation mask, top_pct 1.0, zero cost, and the same residual events as the sleeves (the M4.8 registration v3 secondary benchmark)
benchmarks.factor_etf_blend: Not run: it needs an ETF data source, an owner item.
benchmarks.reported: for R0, rule R1, R2, and each sleeve, per segment and cost case: the annualized mean monthly net excess over SPY and over the equal-weight benchmark, and the compounded excess total return over each, each printed beside the segment's unpriced share

metrics.sharpe_long_only: For every long-only step 4 book (R0, rule R1, R2, each sleeve, the equal-weight benchmark, and SPY): Sharpe = 12 * mean over the window of (r_net,t - RF_t), divided by sqrt(12) * the sample standard deviation (ddof 1) of r_net,t, with RF_t the French FF3 monthly RF of month t. A zero volatility leaves the Sharpe undefined.
metrics.sharpe_public: The public long-short counterparts (jkp_factors_153 R0, R1, and R2) keep the v1 Sharpe without risk-free subtraction, because they are zero-investment returns (v1 baselines.label).
metrics.per_rule: the other research/m5_factor_baseline.py performance metrics on monthly net returns of each comparison window: annualized mean, volatility, maximum drawdown on cumprod(1 + r_net) rebased to 1 at the window start, worst 12-month return, and average monthly turnover; its Sharpe is replaced by sharpe_long_only
metrics.per_sleeve: the same metrics on sleeve months, plus the average monthly stock turnover and cost

survival.primary: The count of the 8 conditions that hold on point-in-time books: 2 segments (pre and post comparison windows) x 2 cost cases x {sharpe_long_only at least, maximum-drawdown magnitude at most}, with research/m5_step3.py closure_conditions and not_worse (differences below 1e-12 in magnitude count as equal; an undefined value fails), called through an adapter that maps the comparator rule, the two segments, and the two cost cases onto its grid keys. It is computed for rule R1 against R0 and for R2 against rule R1 (and for R2 against R0 when R0 is the point-in-time baseline).
survival.public_counterpart: Beside each condition, the same condition on the public jkp_factors_153 books over the same calendar months: step 2 R0 and R1 and step 3 R2, from their continuous public runs with the pinned inputs, at 20 bp beside the primary case and 50 bp beside the sensitivity case, with metrics rebased to each comparison window and the v1 Sharpe (metrics.sharpe_public).
survival.ratio: Beside each condition, the point-in-time margin divided by the public margin when the public margin is positive; otherwise the ratio is reported as undefined. Each margin uses its own book's Sharpe definition.
survival.role: The survival count and ratios are the figure the owner uses before step 4b and step 5. The decision outcomes below use the point-in-time conditions only.

transmission.role: descriptive only; no test and no decision
transmission.sleeve: For each sleeve, over its sleeve months through 2025-12 in each segment and pooled, at the primary cost case: the mean monthly net active return, the mean monthly return of its matched JKP characteristic in the same calendar months, their ratio (undefined when the JKP mean is 0), and their Pearson correlation.
transmission.class: For each of the four themes, over the comparison months: the mean monthly class return minus the equal-weight benchmark return, the mean of the amendment 3 class return r_k,t of that JKP cluster in the same months, their ratio, and their correlation.

halves_and_window.halves: The two segments are the halves: pre [2014-04-30, 2019-06-28] and post [2021-08-31, 2026-08-07]. Each is a separate run that starts from cash; nothing carries across the seal window and its buffers.
halves_and_window.comparison_window: Rule comparisons, survival, S4 tests, and class transmission use the comparison months from the class-layer start to 2019-06 (pre) and to 2025-12 (post). 2025-12 is the last month of the public counterpart (the last JKP month in reports/m5_public_data_manifest.json), so every rule comparison and its public counterpart use the same months. Expected from the calendar alone: 55 pre and 44 post comparison months, 99 in all.
halves_and_window.descriptive_months: Sleeve months 2026-01 to 2026-07 are reported for sleeves and benchmarks only.

tests.statistic: d_t = rule R1 net return minus R0 net return at the primary cost case over the pooled comparison months of both segments, in time order, in the primary run
d_t = R2 net return minus rule R1 net return at the primary cost case over the same months, in the primary run

step4_tests.method: research/m5_step3.py rule_test: src/features/multiple_testing.py return_test_statistics(d, periods_per_year = 12), two-sided HAC p-value, Bartlett lag floor(4 * (n / 100) ** (2 / 9)), and the pointwise 95 percent interval mean +/- 1.959964 * sqrt(LRV / n). The pooled series joins the two segments; the HAC treats the last pre month and the first post month as adjacent. An undefined test keeps its slot with p = 1. The difference is a difference of returns, so the risk-free rate cancels.
step4_tests.last_close_rerun: The rerun reports the mean of each d_t and its sign only; it computes no test statistic, so it adds no slot.
step4_tests.correction: src/features/multiple_testing.py adjust_pvalues(p, method = 'by', family_size = 480) on the 2 observed S4 p-values; the other 478 slots enter as p = 1 through family_size.

family_size.counting_rule: Conservative: the 2 observed tests; one slot at p = 1 for each public rule test of steps 2 and 3; and one slot at p = 1 for every Family A test statistic in the committed M4.7 v1 and v2 records, where the HAC and the iid statistic of one series count separately and every sample (full window and halves), book, and cost case counts separately.

items.variant: S2.jkp_factors_153, S2.jkp_themes_13, S2.french_7, S3.R2, S3.R3, S3.R4
Family A monthly rank IC tests: 6 factors x {HAC, iid}
Family A book return tests: 6 factors x {long_short, long_only} x {primary, sensitivity_2x, zero_cost_diagnostic_only} x {full, first half, second half} x {HAC, iid}
Family A deflated Sharpe values (dsr.A, 6) and Family A PBO (cpcv.A_excess, cpcv.A_long_short, 2)
Family A monthly rank IC tests: 6 factors x {HAC, iid}
Family A book return tests: 6 factors x 2 books x 3 cost cases x 3 samples x {HAC, iid}

required_tests: future_perturbation: on a synthetic fixture, for each of the six signals, changing any price, volume, or membership value after signal row r - 1 leaves the sleeve's target at row r unchanged; changing any sleeve daily return after the last trading day of month t-2, or any public input after its window, leaves month t's sigma and R0, rule R1, and R2 weights unchanged; changing a return on the last trading day of month t-2 can change them (HIGH_52W, LOW_BETA_252, and AMIHUD_ILLIQ_63 have no such test today)

r4_events: a residual held stop settles at -1 at its stop row in every sleeve that holds it and in the equal-weight benchmark, a book not holding it is unaffected, and the last-close copy settles the same stops at 0; a seal-gap piece ending before the last book row becomes a stop at -1 and is counted as a seal-gap stop

affected_event_weights: on a fixture where one sleeve grows 20 percent before an event while the others stay flat, and one event is held by two sleeves, the rule-level incoming weight uses the drifted pre-event sleeve shares, the shared event counts once at rule level and twice as sleeve-event incidences, and the sums and maxima match a hand count

terminal_free_loader: with no terminal/ directory and a sentinel that rejects every read of a path under terminal/ and every call of read_engine_events, bind_step4 and load_segment_runs_step4 load the segments, keep the inventory, split-source, and seal checks, and give each segment an empty event frame; no file is created in the snapshot

fragility: a fixture whose S4 mean, closure margin, or decision outcome changes sign between the two runs is labeled fragile; one whose signs all agree is not; a margin below 1e-12 in magnitude counts as 0; the rerun computes no S4 p-value

long_only_sharpe: on a fixture where the lower-volatility book has the higher mean/volatility ratio without RF but the lower (mean - RF)/volatility ratio with a positive RF, the Sharpe condition fails; the public counterpart's Sharpe equals the v1 no-RF value; a missing RF month refuses
drift_turnover: drift-adjusted class turnover and the switch cost match a hand calculation, with turnover 1 in the first comparison month of each segment

monthly_compounding: a sleeve month compounds its daily net returns over (last trading day of t-1, last trading day of t]; the first sleeve month includes the first reset row's cost; the partial final month enters no monthly figure

own_sigma: ddof 1 over exactly 126 rows of the sleeve's own daily net return ending on the last trading day of t-2; changing the equal-weight benchmark's returns leaves sigma unchanged; 125 rows leave the month without a rule R1 weight; the class layer starts at the first month with a full window for every sleeve; a zero sigma refuses
r2_multipliers: step 4 R2 multipliers equal research/m5_step3.py r2_on_months output for the four themes; R2 weights are positive and sum to 1; a missing multiplier in a comparison month refuses
empty_sleeve_refuses: a rebalance with no eligible member holding a finite signal refuses the run
halt_versus_bad_data: an absent bar of a held asset is a halt under halt_gap_return_v1, while a present non-finite or non-positive close refuses

unpriced_accounting: on a fixture with a resolved priced interval, a resolved interval without a side panel, an unresolved interval with no permanent ID and no bars, a blank exit class, and two overlapping intervals of one code, the member-days, the unresolved_no_permanent_id and unknown buckets, the reason split, and the reconciliation match a hand count; a non-reconciling total refuses; signal exclusions and halt rows are split by exit class

seal_and_pins: a panel row in the seal window refuses seal_bracket_computation_forbidden; a changed manifest, inventory, discovery-inputs, seal carry, build manifest, interval CSV, interval results, security master, or panel hash refuses before any panel load; a seal carry window different from [2019-07-31, 2020-07-31) refuses holdout_overlap_refused
no_snapshot_write: a run on a synthetic snapshot leaves the SHA-256 of every file under its root unchanged
comparison_window: rule comparisons end at the last month of the public counterpart; later sleeve months are descriptive

decision_outcomes: through the closure adapter, a fixture where rule R1 fails any one of its 8 conditions against R0 makes R0 the baseline; one where R2 fails any one of its 8 against rule R1 closes the line; with R0 as baseline, R2 passing against rule R1 but failing one condition against R0 closes the line; an undefined Sharpe fails; a difference below 1e-12 holds
survival_tables: the public counterpart uses the same calendar months with metrics rebased to each window, and the ratio is undefined when the public margin is not positive
transmission: ratio and correlation match a hand calculation, and the ratio is undefined when the JKP mean is 0
s4_family: adjust_pvalues receives 2 observed p-values and family_size 480; any other count refuses
costs: sleeve stock costs come from run_book at 1 + 4 and 2 + 8 bp and pair with 20 and 50 bp switch costs
trial_file_pins: the runner refuses when v1 or any of amendments 1 to 4 differs from its pinned SHA-256 or from HEAD
technical_defaults: File name amendment_4: it follows the existing amendment sequence.
real_v2 only: it covers both segments under partition rule v2, and its post side serves the same acquisitions as real_v1.

The six Family A signals are the price classes, mapped to the JKP cluster of their nearest JKP characteristic: they are the frozen price signals the snapshot supports, and the map makes each comparable with a public series.
Class return = rule R1 within the class on the sleeves, descriptive only: the same definition as amendment 3.
Top quintile, ceil(0.2 n) names, equal weight, the engine's stable order at ties: the roadmap's top-quintile book with the existing engine selection.

Month-end rebalance on the engine's after-close contract; the monthly return compounds daily net returns; the first sleeve month includes the initial purchase cost; the partial month 2026-08 is excluded: monthly returns that match the public calendar months and drop no cost.
A terminal-free segment loader: load_segment_runs without read_engine_events and with empty event frames, because step 4 accepts no terminal evidence (GPT-S4-FR1-A1, OPUS-S4F-A2).
An empty sleeve target refuses the run: otherwise the sleeve silently holds cash (R6).

Unpriced member-days are counted over the segment's reset-to-last-book rows against every interval in the pinned interval results, with unresolved_no_permanent_id and unknown buckets and a reconciliation that refuses on a gap: the unpriced share cannot hide an unresolved case (GPT-S4-FR1-A2, OPUS-S4F-A1).
Stock costs 1 + 4 bp primary and 2 + 8 bp sensitivity: the M4.7 and M4.8 registered cases; no zero-cost sleeve, because it changes no decision (R8).

Class switch cost 20 and 50 bp on drift-adjusted class turnover, paired with the stock cost cases as (1 + 4, 20) and (2 + 8, 50): the v1 levels on the turnover a long-only book actually trades; the v1 no-drift convention rests on long-short returns having no position drift.

Rule R1 sigma is the ddof-1 standard deviation of the sleeve's own daily net return over the 126 US trading days ending on the last trading day of month t-2: step 2's rule with only the window changed, because the v1 window (36 months, at least 24 observations) would leave about 64 of about 99 comparison months; no active-risk or other variant is run (OPUS-S4F-M2 option a).
The class layer starts at the first month with a full sigma window for every sleeve, and R0, rule R1, and R2 start together from cash: every comparison uses the same months and costs.
R2 uses the step 3 multipliers unchanged, from the pinned public inputs: re-estimating on about ten years of stock-level data would leave lambda near 0.

The long-only Sharpe subtracts the French FF3 monthly RF from the net return, and the public long-short counterparts keep the v1 Sharpe: a fully invested book earns the cash rate, and omitting it favors the lower-volatility book (OPUS-S4F-M1).
Rule comparisons end at 2025-12, the last month of the public counterpart, so every comparison and its counterpart use the same months; later sleeve months are descriptive (OPUS-S4F-A5).
The halves are the two segments, each a separate run from cash: the seal window and its buffers separate them.

Survival counts the 8 step 2 conditions with the 1e-12 tolerance, beside the same conditions on the public jkp_factors_153 books over the same months, with the ratio when the public margin is positive: the same bar that chose the public baseline.
Transmission compares each sleeve with its matched JKP characteristic and each class with its amendment 3 class return: the public series each maps to.
S4 tests use rule_test on the pooled comparison months at the primary cost case in the primary run: the step 3 rule test on all step 4 months.

The S4 BY family is 480: 2 observed tests, 6 public rule-test slots, and 472 committed M4.7 Family A statistics at p = 1, counting HAC and iid separately: an inclusive count with each exclusion stated.
No random-date null: the span is too short and step 4 makes no state claim.

Residual held stops, seal-gap stops included, settle at -100 percent in every sleeve and the equal-weight benchmark, with a last-close rerun that reports means and signs only and a sign-based fragility label: the R4 unknown-cause default and rerun set by the coordinator scope defaults of 2026-09-29 (OPUS-S4F-A3, A6, A7).

With R0 as the point-in-time baseline, R2 must also meet the 8 conditions against R0 to continue: the timing line is judged against the baseline product, and this adds a condition without removing one.

Affected events are reported per book as a count and the sum and maximum of incoming weights at the close before the stop; at rule level the sleeve shares drift from the month's targets, and each event counts once, with sleeve-event incidences beside it (GPT-S4-FR1-A3).
The pooled S4 HAC treats the segment boundary as adjacent: one series per test, with the effect stated as a limitation.
Rule and sleeve metrics use research/m5_factor_baseline.py performance on monthly net returns, with the long-only Sharpe in place of its Sharpe: the step 2 metrics, comparable with the public books.
limitations: Every result is DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY and rests on premise VP-2 (O-9); the M4.8 census measured S_D > 0.05 on 22.5 percent of eligible member-days.

No terminal evidence is accepted: every residual held stop, seal-gap stops included, settles at -100 percent, a lower bound for long books that also lowers the equal-weight benchmark; the last-close rerun bounds the other side, and a sign flip labels the result fragile.

Members without a side panel and unresolved intervals are never held (111 of 448 members at D0_pre lack a pre-side panel), so they are outside the R4 affected-event count; if they differ systematically, the universe tilts. The comparisons share the universe, so the effect is second order for the decisions and first order for the excess figures, which print the unpriced share beside them.
The seal window and its buffers exclude 2019-07 to 2021-08, including the 2020 crash, so drawdowns are understated.
About 99 comparison months give little power; the pooled HAC treats the segment boundary as adjacent; monthly drawdowns understate intra-month drawdowns.

The post segment re-examines M4.7 factors and months on the same acquisitions, the pre segment overlaps the static cohort from 2016-08-08 and the CSV validation from 2018-01-02, and only 2014-05 to 2016-07 is unexposed; no result is confirmatory.
All six source papers predate 2014, so every step 4 month is post-publication.
R2's multipliers come from public long-short data and are not re-estimated on stock-level books.
Rule R1 uses a 126-day sigma, not the v1 36-month window; it is the same risk measure over a shorter window, which may be noisier.
The long-only Sharpe subtracts RF and the public long-short Sharpe does not, so the survival ratio compares margins under each book's own definition.
Costs do not net across sleeves and include no market-impact model; the switch cost is a proxy for the stock trades a class reweighting needs.
Four of 13 themes are covered; Seasonality and share-based Size wait, and the SEC as-filed classes are step 4b.
The public counterpart is the 153-factor book, not a six-factor public book, so survival compares a narrow stock-level book with a broad public one.
With 480 slots, the smallest S4 p-value needs about 1.5e-5 (HAC |t| about 4.3) to reach BY q 0.05; the prior slots make significance rare, and the report says so.
The S4 prior-slot count covers the committed M4.7 records only; the seal record's CSV validation and historical evaluation and any interactive work left no countable record.
